Faint show-through from the reverse side and a narrow strip of marginal text at the far left edge (partly cut off, not transcribed as notes).

main_text.p: Fœmina habens in vna manu auem & in altera pisce m: si sculpta fuerit in Chrysolito, ad negociandum multum valet.
Lupi figura sculpta in Iaspide contra astu-tiam valet, & infana verba prohibet pro-ferre.
Cerui figura in Iaspide sculpta virtutem ha-bet sanandi & liberandi lunaticos & phre-neticos,
Imperatoris figura in Iaspide sculpta cum capite erecto, gestantem reddit amabilem ab omni creatura, & quicquid petierit, ob-tinebit.
Virginis figura cum veste profusa tenentis in manu laurum, si sculpta fuerit in Iaspide, gestantem efficit securum à submersione a-quæ, necà Dæmone vexabitur, facitq; poten-tem, & omnia impetrantem.
Hominis figura habens in manu inscriptam palmam, si in Iaspide reperiatur, potentem reddit gestantem principibusq; gratum. Ha-ctenus Thetel.
main_text.head: SCVLPTVRÆ SALO-monia.
main_text.p: VEtustissimus inuentus est libellus in de-serto apud filios Israelis, qui quoniā in eo multa

page.notes: Faint show-through text from the reverse page is ignored. The left edge strip of marginal text is cut off and largely illegible. The signature and the catchword "multa" are as printed; the drop-cap V is joined to "Etustissimus" as printed.
